units.data_gb_day: gigabytes generated per day of operations
units.downlink_gb_day: additional downlink capacity added (utility items only)

_meta.design_rule: Every instrument must be a trade-off: nothing here is strictly better than another option at the same budget.

instruments.name: Basic Optical Camera
instruments.blurb: Cheap, light, always fits. Sees weather systems, not individual buildings.
instruments.tradeoff: Lowest science return of any imager — fine for a first mission, not for a science objective.

instruments.name: High-Resolution Multispectral Camera
instruments.blurb: The workhorse of Earth observation. 10 m ground sampling in 8 bands.
instruments.tradeoff: 20 GB/day forces a serious downlink budget.

instruments.name: Stereo / 3D Imager
instruments.blurb: Two cameras, one DEM. Measures terrain height and change.
instruments.tradeoff: Biggest data producer per unit of science — needs Ka-band or a relay.

instruments.name: SAR Radar Imager
instruments.blurb: Sees through cloud and darkness. Floods, subsidence, sea ice.
instruments.tradeoff: 180 W is a power plant problem, not an instrument problem.

instruments.name: LiDAR Altimeter
instruments.blurb: Centimetre-precision surface height. Ice sheets and oceans.
instruments.tradeoff: Only useful if your orbit actually repeats its ground track.

instruments.name: VNIR Spectrometer
instruments.blurb: Identifies materials from their reflected spectrum.
instruments.tradeoff: Needs sunlight — useless at night or in eclipse.

instruments.name: Thermal IR Sounder
instruments.blurb: Temperature and humidity profiles. Works day and night.
instruments.tradeoff: Detector must be cooled — power and radiator area both climb.

instruments.name: Microwave Radiometer
instruments.tradeoff: Large antenna aperture — mass lives in the structure, not the sensor.

instruments.name: Magnetometer
instruments.blurb: Tiny, cheap, barely drinks power. Maps the magnetic field.
instruments.tradeoff: Almost free — but magnetic cleanliness requirements constrain the whole bus.

instruments.name: Plasma Analyzer
instruments.blurb: Measures the charged particles that damage electronics.
instruments.tradeoff: Highly valuable in MEO/GEO where radiation is the risk.

instruments.name: Space Telescope (0.3 m)
instruments.blurb: The highest science value in the catalogue.
instruments.tradeoff: 210 kg + 300 W + 55M — it defines the entire mission around itself.

instruments.name: Ka-band High-Gain Terminal
instruments.blurb: Not science — it buys you downlink capacity (+45 GB/day).
instruments.tradeoff: Pure enabler: mass, power and money spent on moving data instead of making it.

bus_options._note: The spacecraft platform. Pick exactly one power source and one battery.

power.name: Deployable Solar Array — Small (5 m²)
power.blurb: Cheap and light, but 90 W total generation — leave room for eclipse.
power.tradeoff: Cannot support SAR or a telescope.

power.name: Deployable Solar Array — Medium (15 m²)
power.blurb: The balanced choice: enough for most instrument suites.
power.tradeoff: 60 kg of your launch capacity gone before you pick a single instrument.

power.name: Deployable Solar Array — Large (30 m²)
power.tradeoff: Dominates the mass budget; drag in LEO shortens lifetime.

power.name: Radioisotope Generator (RTG)
power.blurb: Works in eclipse and at any distance from the Sun.
power.tradeoff: 45M for 120 W, and it decays: -0.8% power per year.

battery.name: Battery Pack — 400 Wh
battery.blurb: Covers a 35-minute eclipse for a light spacecraft.

battery.name: Battery Pack — 1200 Wh
battery.blurb: Standard for LEO with imaging payloads.

battery.name: Battery Pack — 3000 Wh
battery.blurb: For high-draw payloads that must run through eclipse.
battery.tradeoff: 70 kg is two instruments' worth of mass.

bus.name: Small Satellite Bus (150 kg class)
bus.blurb: Structure, ADCS, OBC, thermal for a 150 kg satellite.

bus.name: Medium Satellite Bus (500 kg class)
bus.blurb: Room for a real instrument suite.

bus.name: Large Satellite Bus (1500 kg class)
bus.blurb: Everything fits — and so does the bill.

engineering_rules.note: Rule of thumb used by real mission designers: dry mass + 15% margin must fit the launcher.
